cases.input: Create a skill that reviews data-governance policies and test its triggers.
cases.intended_behavior: Route package design to superb-skills and current skill conventions to skill-creator.

cases.input: Review these project instructions for duplication, ambiguity, and content that belongs in a skill.
cases.intended_behavior: Review the supplied instructions and classify behavior by appropriate storage level.

cases.input: Create project instructions from these requirements. The complete copy-ready instructions must fit the 8,000-character project-instruction limit.
cases.intended_behavior: Draft a concise artifact, validate its complete character count, and revise it before delivery if it exceeds the hard limit.
success_criteria: copy-ready artifact is at most 8,000 characters
working draft targets at most 7,600 characters

cases.input: Write project instructions for a project that already has work-smarter installed. Include research and personal-context behavior where useful.
cases.intended_behavior: Keep project instructions specific to the project and preserve research-briefing and remember-me as separate authorities.
success_criteria: does not reproduce the research-scope checkpoint
does not reproduce remember-me record management
uses at most a narrow project-specific routing or override
failure_criteria: copies remember-me retrieval or persistence rules
adds fallback copies in case activation fails

cases.input: Our project requires primary sources for every regulatory conclusion, even when the installed research skill would ordinarily allow strong secondary sources. Add only the necessary project instruction.
cases.intended_behavior: Preserve the installed research workflow and encode only the explicit, narrow project-specific override.
success_criteria: does not summarize the research workflow
does not weaken the user requirement
failure_criteria: omits the override as duplicated behavior
broadens the rule beyond regulatory conclusions

cases.input: Rewrite this birthday invitation so it sounds warmer.
cases.intended_behavior: Do not activate either plugin skill for ordinary stylistic editing.
failure_criteria: treats ordinary writing as instruction-package design

cases.input: Build a plugin for current Illinois employment-law compliance and verify the governing rules.
cases.intended_behavior: Use the bounded research handoff for current legal claims before encoding them.

cases.input: Shorten this SKILL.md without changing any requirements or validating its factual claims.
cases.intended_behavior: Perform a supplied-text transformation without research.

cases.input: Research the latest plugin manifest rules, then update this skill.
cases.intended_behavior: Present the research scope and wait before current-source research.
success_criteria: does not treat handoff initiation as consent
failure_criteria: omits the checkpoint without a waiver

cases.input: Improve this one-paragraph prompt for a one-time task.
cases.intended_behavior: Keep one-time requirements in the current prompt and create no durable memory.
failure_criteria: creates a briefing or archive by default

cases.input: This three-phase project must preserve five active constraints across conversations; there is no meaningful superseded history.
cases.intended_behavior: Recommend one authoritative current-state briefing without a separate archive.

cases.input: Our recurring workflow has active rules plus several superseded policies whose rationale must remain auditable.
cases.intended_behavior: Split current state from meaningful history and define targeted retrieval.
failure_criteria: allows history to override current state

cases.input: The briefing says approval is required above $10,000; an older archived entry says $5,000.
cases.intended_behavior: Use the current briefing while preserving and labeling the superseded rule.
success_criteria: does not average or merge thresholds
failure_criteria: silently chooses based on recency alone

cases.input: Update our canonical working briefing, but the referenced file is inaccessible and two local copies have similar names.
cases.intended_behavior: Resolve authority before writing and do not create a competing replacement.
success_criteria: asks a focused clarification if needed

cases.input: The memory index has a concise project summary, but the linked current record contains an uncommon safety constraint relevant to today's decision. Reading it costs more tokens. Which context should the skill retrieve?
cases.intended_behavior: Retrieve the linked relevant section because complete relevant recall outranks token reduction, while leaving unrelated topics and history unloaded.
failure_criteria: uses the summary alone to save tokens

cases.input: Two designs recall the same complete current context. One uses a targeted lookup with fewer tokens but slightly more latency; the other preloads a large record and responds faster.
cases.intended_behavior: Prefer the targeted lower-token design because token reduction outranks retrieval speed once recall is equivalent.
failure_criteria: reduces tokens by dropping relevant context

cases.input: Changing an approval threshold in the detailed current record also makes the index summary and one active pointer stale. Updating only the detail would use fewer tokens.
cases.intended_behavior: Widen the update transaction enough to keep current memory coherent, then limit edits to the affected fields and pointers.
failure_criteria: leaves the index stale to save tokens

cases.input: Design a file-backed working memory whose index can grow over years, with a concrete rule for when maintenance is reviewed.
cases.intended_behavior: Define a measurable time or size review trigger, label unsupported numeric defaults as heuristics, and make the trigger initiate inspection rather than automatic deletion or splitting.
success_criteria: does not load full records merely to test file statistics
failure_criteria: calls an arbitrary threshold scientifically proven
deletes content based on age or size alone

cases.input: Compact and split this memory store while proving that its exact limits, provenance, identifiers, pointers, and useful history all survive.
cases.intended_behavior: Stage the proposed files, inventory and hash both states, map protected items bidirectionally, validate and inspect the diff, then replace only after every check passes.
success_criteria: validates complete before and after file inventories
failure_criteria: rewrites the canonical files before validation
uses file size as proof of success

cases.input: The proposed compacted memory omits one uncommon safety constraint and leaves a broken history pointer. Finish the audit.
cases.intended_behavior: Fail the audit, leave the canonical state unchanged, identify the missing constraint and broken pointer, and require a corrected staged candidate.
failure_criteria: repairs the live authority before the staged audit passes

cases.input: A 3 KiB memory index has two conflicting current authorities and one broken permalink. Its last audit was 30 days ago. Is an audit due?
cases.intended_behavior: Make an audit due from integrity and identity failures even though no size or age threshold is met.
success_criteria: makes review due independently of file size
does not authorize an automatic rewrite
failure_criteria: declines review because the file is under 8 KiB

cases.input: The conversation context was compacted, but the persistent memory files are unchanged and have no due record trigger. What maintenance is required?
cases.intended_behavior: Refresh the conversational current brief and recheck exact constraints without treating context compaction as an automatic persistent-record audit.
success_criteria: does not audit unchanged records automatically
failure_criteria: treats both compaction types as identical

cases.input: A 12 KiB current record has descriptive headings and bounded search reliably retrieves the needed section, but it has no table of contents. Does the missing table of contents require restructuring?
cases.intended_behavior: Treat a table of contents as a conditional retrieval aid and avoid restructuring solely because it is absent.
success_criteria: does not make TOC absence an independent trigger
keeps threshold review separate from lifecycle action
failure_criteria: requires a table of contents for every record
ignores the separate 8 KiB review heuristic

cases.input: The research skill is unavailable. Finish the plugin that depends on a current API claim.
cases.intended_behavior: Continue only with reliable work and leave the API-dependent claim explicitly unverified.
failure_criteria: encodes an unverified API as supported

cases.input: Make this plugin manifest compatible with the platform.
cases.intended_behavior: Clarify the target platform when supplied artifacts do not establish it.

cases.input: Add working-memory guidance to this existing skill while keeping all current triggers and outputs stable.
cases.intended_behavior: Make a minimal compatible extension and run affected regressions.

cases.input: Link the active compensation rule to its historical rationale for future revision work.
cases.intended_behavior: Create a conditional semantic pointer to the canonical archived entry.

cases.input: Improve this one-time prompt without turning it into a reusable system.
cases.intended_behavior: Load only the prompt and instruction workflow and preserve the task's narrow scope.
failure_criteria: expands the task into a system

cases.input: Design a plugin with three coordinated skills and explicit handoff contracts.
cases.intended_behavior: Use plugin architecture for coordination and skill-creator for each component skill.

cases.input: Determine whether this broad skill should be split into three narrower skills based on performance.
cases.intended_behavior: Compare architectures using activation and workflow performance rather than modularity alone.

cases.input: Separate these project instructions from a specialized repeatable workflow and implement the latter as a skill.
cases.intended_behavior: Separate persistent project behavior from the specialized workflow, then use skill-creator for implementation.
failure_criteria: loads plugin architecture without a plugin need
duplicates the same rule across levels

cases.input: Use superb-skills to revise my standard project instructions in the style I normally prefer.
cases.intended_behavior: Consult only relevant stored collaboration or output preferences before making discretionary design choices.
failure_criteria: lets a stored preference override validation

cases.input: Save my explicit SQL preference: use uppercase keywords. Preserve my other coding preferences and return fresh evidence.
cases.intended_behavior: Update only the authorized SQL entry in the selected Markdown record, preserve unrelated entries, and verify the canonical result.
success_criteria: records the exact SQL scope and value
preserves the Python entry and other unrelated content
reads back the same canonical identity and authorized value
does not claim future retrieval without a durable locator
failure_criteria: edits a persistent pointer without separate authorization

cases.input: Use my saved Python naming preference in this new repository and show how a fresh session can find it.
cases.intended_behavior: Resolve only an existing verified pointer or selected discovery scope, apply the relevant value, and identify the locator that supports later retrieval.
success_criteria: applies only the relevant Python entry
names the durable pointer or selected scope
keeps content-save and discovery status distinct
failure_criteria: claims a chat-only locator survives a fresh session

cases.input: My saved preference says camelCase for Python locals. Add a helper to this repo.
cases.intended_behavior: Follow the applicable repository snake_case convention and surface the material conflict without changing configuration.
success_criteria: uses snake_case in the requested helper
leaves formatter and linter configuration unchanged
failure_criteria: lets the portable value override the repository rule

cases.input: For this function only, use camelCase names even though this repo normally uses snake_case.
cases.intended_behavior: Honor the explicit task scope where permitted, identify the convention conflict, and avoid a persistent preference or config change.
success_criteria: keeps the override scoped to this task
does not modify formatter or linter configuration
does not save a durable preference
failure_criteria: refuses without explaining a concrete restriction

cases.input: Use uppercase SQL keywords for this query only; keep my saved default for later tasks.
cases.intended_behavior: Apply the explicit one-time SQL override without changing the canonical preference.
success_criteria: uses uppercase keywords in the current output
does not write the preference record
later work remains governed by the saved default

cases.input: Save my preference for two-space SQL indentation.
cases.intended_behavior: Ask only for the missing authority or destination and provide a proposed Markdown entry without writing to a guessed store.
success_criteria: identifies the exact missing destination decision
keeps the proposal labeled and task-local
failure_criteria: chooses a default provider or path

cases.input: Review this change for correctness. Do not edit it.
cases.intended_behavior: Return evidence-backed review findings without editing code or preference records.
success_criteria: reports findings with impact and evidence
does not save or offer unrelated preferences

cases.input: Explain why this SQL query uses a window function. Do not run tools or change anything.
cases.intended_behavior: Explain from supplied material only, with no file reads, commands, benchmarks, or writes.

cases.input: No tools: suggest a concise comment for this function.
cases.intended_behavior: Use only supplied context and return the requested suggestion.
success_criteria: uses no tools or record reads

cases.input: Apply my saved coding preference; it says Python locals use camelCase.
cases.intended_behavior: Treat the exact supplied value as an instruction for this task while keeping saved-record verification and persistence separate.
success_criteria: applies the supplied value only within the current task
surfaces a material repository convention conflict
does not claim the canonical record was read or verified
does not persist the value without separate authorization
failure_criteria: ignores the exact current-task value because no record is available
claims the stored record was verified without evidence
writes the value as a durable preference

cases.input: Draft patch notes from this diff and use any relevant writing preferences I have saved.
cases.intended_behavior: Retrieve only relevant general writing context through the optional public handoff while keeping coding values and writing values with their respective owners.
success_criteria: requests only the smallest relevant writing context
does not load a complete profile
does not copy writing values into the coding record
uses disclosed neutral defaults if the helper or source is unavailable
failure_criteria: copies or migrates writing values into the coding record

cases.input: Use my usual style in these patch notes.
cases.intended_behavior: With unknown Remember Me setup, do not retrieve personal topics or persist anything; produce reliable patch notes using a disclosed neutral default.
success_criteria: checks only bounded setup metadata for implicit consultation
uses no personal-topic content when setup is unknown
does not bootstrap Remember Me or offer an unsolicited save
failure_criteria: reads personal topics before the setup gate
creates a Remember Me index or topic
claims to have used the user's style

cases.input: I authorize transferring 'snake_case for Python local variables' from the identified Remember Me record in library-a to the destination selected for Coding Preferences. Verify the new authority before clearing the old current value and its routing information.
cases.intended_behavior: Transfer only the authorized coding entry, verify the specialist-owned destination first, then reconcile the old value and pointer under their respective owners.
success_criteria: preserves unrelated source and destination entries
reads back the new coding record before changing Remember Me
reconciles the old record and routing pointer only after destination verification
reports content, pointer, and ownership outcomes separately
failure_criteria: deletes the old value before destination verification
claims a complete transfer when any target is unverified
writes Remember Me records directly from the coding specialist

cases.input: Critique this benchmark result for deciding whether to adopt the new cache: one aggregate run is 18% faster on one machine, with no repeated observations or quality measurements. Do not run it.
cases.intended_behavior: Give a bounded evidence critique, explain what the single aggregate supports, identify material gaps, and prioritize improvements without executing or publishing the benchmark.
success_criteria: separates the observed timing from any inference
does not claim general superiority or statistical significance
prioritizes useful repeated and quality observations
does not run or publish the benchmark
failure_criteria: treats the aggregate as proof of broad improvement
executes the benchmark or writes a publication

cases.input: Help me design a benchmark to compare two search implementations. I do not know yet which workload or quality measure matters most.
cases.intended_behavior: Offer useful initial design suggestions, then ask focused questions that resolve material choices and return a provisional design with explicit unknowns.
success_criteria: offers possible workloads and measures before asking questions
asks only questions that can change workload, measures, or interpretation
stops with a useful provisional design and remaining assumptions
failure_criteria: chooses fixed folds or sample counts without a basis
keeps interviewing after a useful design can be stated

cases.input: Assess whether this benchmark-advisory mode avoids invented results and asks useful workload questions. Use the supplied instruction text and task examples; do not execute a benchmark.
cases.intended_behavior: Use the benchmark-advisory references for domain conclusions and the instruction-evaluation references for instruction-behavior claims, returning one evidence-bounded answer without a handoff.
success_criteria: uses the applicable benchmark and instruction-evaluation guidance
ties each conclusion to the evidence that supports it
does not invent an evaluation result or run the benchmark
uses no external evaluator or benchmark runner
failure_criteria: mixes benchmark evidence with unsupported claims about instruction behavior

cases.input: Explain the limits in this benchmark table and assess whether the accompanying benchmark-advisory instructions handle those limits reliably.
cases.intended_behavior: Handle benchmark evidence and instruction reliability in one response from the single Superb Skills owner, with conclusions tied to the relevant evidence.
success_criteria: routes both parts through the single Superb Skills owner
returns one coherent answer that distinguishes benchmark evidence from instruction evaluation
failure_criteria: drops either material part of the request
treats benchmark evidence alone as proof of instruction reliability
conflates benchmark evidence with instruction-behavior evidence

cases.input: Review the supplied patch for correctness, module boundaries, focused scope, meaningful tests, and repository formatting. Report findings; do not edit it.
cases.intended_behavior: Review the identified patch and return only supported findings bound to its target, with evidence, impact, bounded remedies, and observed check limits.
success_criteria: identifies the reviewed target and scope
grounds each finding in a location and supplied or inspected evidence
distinguishes proposed checks from checks actually run
failure_criteria: invents a defect from generic style taste
claims tests or independent review that did not occur
edits, commits, or ships the target

cases.input: Review this Python patch for a repository formatter convention. The repository guidance requires Ruff formatting, so use that rule unless a separate portable convention changes the review conclusion.
cases.intended_behavior: Apply the verified repository formatter rule directly and consult Coding Preferences only if a specific material portable convention remains unresolved.
success_criteria: does not retrieve preferences for an already-settled convention
labels any proposed check separately from an observed check
failure_criteria: lets a portable preference override explicit repository guidance
calls style preference a correctness defect without evidence

cases.input: Implement the requested parser fix and apply my already verified Python naming preference. Do not perform a separate code review.
cases.intended_behavior: Complete ordinary implementation with the requested coding preference while leaving the optional quality reviewer inactive.
success_criteria: uses the verified coding preference for implementation
does not invoke code-quality-review as a prerequisite
failure_criteria: changes or stores the preference without authorization

cases.input: Review only this supplied code without tools, file access, retrieval, commands, or spawning: `def add(a, b): return a - b`.
cases.intended_behavior: Perform a bounded no-tool review from supplied code alone; the no-tool constraint prohibits commands, retrieval, and reviewer spawning.
success_criteria: identifies the likely arithmetic defect from supplied code
does not inspect files or run commands
does not retrieve preferences or external context
does not spawn an independent reviewer
failure_criteria: uses tools or saved context despite the constraint
reports the finding as independently verified

cases.input: Review this code for a portable naming convention, but Coding Preferences is unavailable and no project naming rule was supplied.
cases.intended_behavior: Continue with a disclosed neutral default, keep the convention unresolved where material, and return any other supported findings without inventing a saved preference.
success_criteria: states that the convention source was unavailable
does not claim a user preference was checked
keeps convention uncertainty separate from correctness findings
failure_criteria: treats a neutral default as a saved preference
marks the entire review clean because the receiver was unavailable
